# libreac / fuzz_scene

libreac's own fuzz target `fuzz_scene` ([source](source/fuzz_scene.c), unmodified), which OSS-Fuzz does not run, over libreac 1.9.0 (FreeREAC/libreac at d16f3f4e).

Builds a scene body of an input-chosen length (its own allocation) from libreac's placeholder scene XORed with the payload, then calls the scene-push framing on it: reac_ctrl_build_scene_step at an input-chosen step, optionally the whole 343-step transfer, reac_ctrl_scene_set_mac and reac_ctrl_scene_build. A refused body or step is an ordinary result.

## How this program differs from a libFuzzer build of this fuzz target
- Linked against a static libreac.a of every src/*.c of libreac 1.9.0 at commit d16f3f4e, compiled with each build's flags, as libreac's Makefile builds its fuzz targets but with this toolchain in place of a native clang and libFuzzer.
- In every build, getenv() returns NULL, getpid() returns 1 and mkstemp() uses a fixed name, so the program depends only on its input.
- A small driver reads the input file, calls the fuzz target one to four times and prints each return value.

## What the harness checks
- The step builder accepts exactly a body of REAC_SCENE_BYTES and a step in [0, REAC_SCENE_STEPS), refuses everything else, and a refused step writes nothing into the block ([lines 236-254](source/fuzz_scene.c#L236-L254)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- A built step is a cd ea link-1 bulk block whose bytes sum to zero, carries its FIRST, MIDDLE or LAST segment, declares its share of the body and carries the body's bytes at that offset; the LAST step ends with the fixed 12-byte trailer ([lines 83-137](source/fuzz_scene.c#L83-L137)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- reac_ctrl_parse reads every built step back as SCENE_TRANSFER with the link, segment, opcode and length it was built with, and its block checksum check accepts it ([lines 140-163](source/fuzz_scene.c#L140-L163)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- A whole body is accepted at every step, the step payloads concatenated in order are the body byte for byte, and their lengths sum to the total the first step declares ([lines 175-202](source/fuzz_scene.c#L175-L202)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- set_mac and scene_build each accept exactly a REAC_SCENE_BYTES body, and a refused call writes nothing; set_mac writes the MAC at REAC_SCENE_MAC_OFF and nothing else, and scene_build makes the body zeros, the three tags and the MAC ([lines 266-329](source/fuzz_scene.c#L266-L329)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.

| `asan_ubsan_agrees` | on every input on which the plain build is never refused memory for exceeding 2 GiB (a premise): neither build reaches an error and both have the same set of observable behaviours; ASan+UBSan never fires; memory refused only when forced | [proved](proofs/asan_ubsan_agrees/) |

## Builds
Static riscv64 Linux programs, compiled for RV64G and run as `<file> <input-file>`; `oft fetch libreac` downloads the published ones and checks each against its SHA-256.

| build | file | bytes | sha256 |
|---|---|---:|---|
| plain | `fuzz_scene.plain` | 55,016 | `afedb7a7edf00e0ccf3141f3498196bd12feac51cefb72b412c761b9341b1a3f` |
| ubsan | `fuzz_scene.ubsan` | 55,992 | `e9e61c239736db98523e664ee0ebf644b2c1588601a8ef2176633e0aa76f8399` |
| asan | `fuzz_scene.asan` | 579,368 | `43654a025fd02e1f248bcaf6b8ac44f9e5dbded7f2fc1d9a1e90f9d74feb3026` |
| asan-ubsan | `fuzz_scene.asan-ubsan` | 580,184 | `e98b1ed286c1aa5c3d558cb2069011d2413d58b2122f741531364382a528833f` |

Each build also links code that no sanitizer instruments, as its link recorded it. A statement about a sanitizer build covers that code only as uninstrumented code: ASan checks no load or store made inside it, and UBSan inserts no check there.

- plain: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc.a` (the C library)
- ubsan: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc.a` (the C library)
- asan: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.asan.a` (the sanitizer runtime), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc.a` (the C library), `libunwind.a` (the C++ runtime)
- asan-ubsan: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.asan.a` (the sanitizer runtime), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc.a` (the C library), `libunwind.a` (the C++ runtime)
